h: Planning a Day With Little Ride Fans
p: Theme parks with young children are a different game from a day out with teenagers. Small legs tire quickly, attention spans are short, and the best-laid plans can be derailed by one dropped ice cream. The good news is that having Nickelodeon Land as its own area means you can base most of the day in one zone, rather than trailing across the whole park between rides.

Start with the gentle rides to build confidence, then let the little ones decide if they want to try something a bit bolder. Some children will happily ride everything twice, while others need a few goes on the calm ones before they're ready for a wooden coaster. Watching other kids come off grinning is often the best encouragement.

Before you set off, measure your children at home so you've a rough idea which rides they'll be tall enough for. That way, there are no nasty surprises at the front of the queue. Some parks run a rider swap system for families where one adult waits with a child who's too small while the others ride, then swaps over; it's worth asking staff if that's an option on the bigger rides.

Build in proper rest stops. A sit-down for a snack or a drink between rides helps avoid the dreaded afternoon meltdown. When the park gets too much, Blackpool's beach is just over the road from the South Shore, perfect for an hour of sandcastles before heading back for one last go. South Pier is a short stroll away too, and the trams along the prom are a treat for kids in themselves, especially the vintage heritage trams that run on special occasions.
